2	
3	Worktree: `/Users/sully/code_repos/plan-trial/sb-187-stage-investigate-v5lean-haiku-a`, branch `stage/sb-187-investigate-v5lean-haiku-a`, HEAD `7fe8949` (Release 0.4.1). Tree was clean. No file in the repo was edited.

5	Read: `CLAUDE.md` (given), `docs/design.md` (plan review and Dispatch sections: ~1000-1030, 1180-1200, 1620-1640, 1738-1790, 2155-2220, 2525-2545, 3612-3645), `docs/lessons.md` (84 lines; nothing on reruns or revisions, so it adds no constraint here). Read the code paths listed below in full.
6	
7	## Summary
8	
9	The bug is in the code, not the issue reporter's setup. A plan-review rerun copies its input from the newest **Complete** attempt that has a `plan` artifact. A review attempt that failed with `review run gone` is never Complete, so the rerun takes `plan/1`. The owner's `revise` lives in two places that the rerun never reads: the revised copy in `review/1/joined/plan.md`, and the owner's round file `review/1/joined/plan.feedback-<n>.md` (with a `Revision` entry on `review/1`). The `rerun` note path also drops everything for a workflow stage. `show` prints only the newest workflow attempt's copy, so the lost revision is not named anywhere.
10	
11	## Code that the issue touches (this tree)
12	
13	### 1. The failure: `review run gone`
14	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7741-7790` `poll_workflow`: asks the app `Body::Workflow { run }` (7753). On `Reply::Failed` with `NO_SUCH_RUN` (7755) it calls `fail_attempt` with `review run gone: no such run` (7761).
15	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:8445` `NO_SUCH_RUN = "no such run"`.
16	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7148-7158` `fail_attempt` → `fail_attempt_with(... &["rerun", "park"])`. Failure reason is stored on the attempt; state becomes `Failed`.
17	- App side: `src/app.rs:3915-3919` answers `Body::Workflow` from `core.run_view(WorkflowId)`; `None` → `"no such run"`. `src/core/control.rs:865` `run_view`; `src/core/workflow.rs:222` `workflow(id)` looks in `self.workflows()`. Runs are persisted in the project record: `src/core/model.rs:337` (`WorkflowRun`), `src/adapters/store.rs:1454` (`workflows: Vec<WorkflowRun>`).
18	
19	### 2. The rerun question
20	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7308-7332` `ask_rerun` → `rerun_ask` at `9335-9377`. The question reads `"<stage> (<ctx>) attempt <n> failed: <reason>. Run it again?"` plus `rerun_carries` (9382-9390), which returns `""` for a workflow stage. The question says nothing about which copy will be reviewed.
21	- `scheduler.rs:9382-9390` `rerun_carries`: carry text only for `AttemptKind::Review` (code review), not plan review.
22	
23	### 3. The rerun decision and the note
24	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:3524-3530`: the `("rerun", "rerun")` arm reads `rerun_note(t, p, i)` then `retire_replaced(...)`.
25	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:8988-9013` `rerun_note`: returns `None` unless the stage kind is `Agent` or `Review` (8993-8997). A plan review is `StageKind::Workflow` (`dispatch/src/pipeline.rs:715-725`, `kind()`), so the `rerun` answer's own note is discarded for a plan review, and nothing is put into `t.rework`.
26	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:10599-10601` `sent_back`: "A workflow stage takes no note."
27	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:3578-3605` `retire_replaced`: marks the decision acted, saves, unmarks. It deletes no directory.
28	
29	### 4. The rerun itself
30	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7379-7434` `workflow_stage`: for a latest attempt that is not open and not Complete, `may_rerun` (7402) → `start_workflow(... next_n ...)`.
31	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7436-7530` `start_workflow`:
32	  - 7465-7470: `review_subject(t, &subject)` gives `(source_path, source_session)`.
33	  - 7471-7472: `std::fs::copy(&source_path, &copy)` where `copy = <attempt dir>/plan.md`, a new file under `review/<n>/joined/`. Note the new attempt is `n = next_n`, so attempt 2 gets `review/2/joined/plan.md`.
34	  - 7480-7487: `new_attempt(... AttemptState::Starting, BTreeMap::from([(subject, copy)]))`.
35	  - 7510-7520: `Body::WorkflowStart { source: source_session, plan: copy, ... }`.
36	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:10534-10548` `review_subject`: `t.attempts.iter().rev().filter(|a| a.state == AttemptState::Complete)` → first attempt with artifact `subject`; returns that attempt's path and `a.session`. 37	
38	### 5. The revise path (where the owner's note goes)
39	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:3495-3498`: `("finalize", "revise")` → `revise(...)` then `unmark`.
40	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7565-7650` `revise`:
41	  - needs the run to be `Converged` or `AtCap` (7589-7603 region);
42	  - `round = view.round + 1`; `file = crate::report::round_file(&subject, round)` at 7616: `<stem>.feedback-<n>.md` **beside the reviewed copy**, i.e. `review/1/joined/plan.feedback-<round>.md`;
43	  - writes `"<OWNER_ROUND_HEADING>\n\n<note>"` with `atomic_write` (7617-7618);
44	  - `review.revisions.push(Revision { round, by, at_ms })` at 7621 on the attempt (`review/1`);
45	  - sends `Body::WorkflowObject { run, round, text }` (REVISE) to the app. On refusal it removes the file (7642).

47	- `dispatch/src/report.rs:151-158` `round_file` / `beside`; `report.rs:165` `plan_round_numbers` lists the files that exist.
48	- `dispatch/src/lib.rs:102` `revisable` (finalize/revise pair); `lib.rs:95` mentions `revisions`.

50	### 6. The revised copy
51	- The copy is `review/1/joined/plan.md`, the attempt's `artifacts["plan"]` (set in `start_workflow`'s `new_attempt` for attempt 1). Per `docs/design.md:2213-2216`, the review edits its copy in place under that one path. Nothing in the tree copies it out at revise time, and nothing reads it after the attempt fails.
52	- The app keeps round snapshots at `<data dir>/workflows/<run>/round-<n>/` (`src/core/workflow.rs:41`), per `docs/design.md:1000-1030`. Dispatch does not read them.

54	### 7. The readers that disagree (the core of the bug)
55	| Reader | Rule | Location |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| Agent inputs (`input`, `input_where`, `lane_input`, `lane_plan`) | newest **Complete**, not forgotten | `ticket.rs:1437-1462`; `scheduler.rs:10843-10856` |
58	| Display (`shown`, `shown_where`, `shown_lane_files`) | newest Complete, or an **open** Workflow attempt | `ticket.rs:1467-1490`; `scheduler.rs:10900-10960` |
59	| Plan-review rerun source (`review_subject`) | newest **Complete** with artifact, plus its session | `scheduler.rs:10534-10548` |

61	The existing unit test `ticket.rs:1827-1875` (`the_plan_shown_is_an_open_review_copy_but_an_input_never_is`) asserts that a Cancelled or Failed review copy is **not** shown as the plan (1856-1864: "A parked review's copy is not the plan going forward"). So "failed" and "parked" are treated the same by the current design. A fix that makes the failed copy the rerun's input must change that rule or add a distinction; the test is the constraint the planner has to face. The first test, `ticket.rs:1797`, asserts that a Failed plan attempt's input is skipped.

63	Note on the session: `poll_workflow` writes the card's face into `Attempt.session` (`scheduler.rs:7784-7788`: `view.planner` or `view.reviewer`). 66	- `dispatch/src/main.rs:911-997` `show`. The `files:` block is at 980-995:

83	  - `review/1/joined/plan.md`: the copy of the plan at review start, edited in place by the review run, containing the revision. `review/1` is `Failed` with reason `review run gone: no such run`.

85	  - `review/1` `revisions`: `[{round: 2, by: "you", at_ms}]`.
86	  - `review/2/joined/plan.md`: fresh copy of `plan/1/joined/plan.md` made by `start_workflow` (7471).
87	- App side: the `WorkflowRun` in the project record of the Switchboard app's store (`src/core/model.rs:337`; persisted, `src/adapters/store.rs:1454`). It holds `plan` path, `rounds`, `state`, and round snapshots under `<data dir>/workflows/<run>/`.

90	- The runner loads the ticket record and sees `review/1` as an open attempt with `run` set. `poll_workflow` asks the app. The app's answer is `no such run` (the issue's report). 96	```
97	files:
98	  plan: <data>/tickets/<id>/review/2/joined/plan.md
99	    (reviewed copy, review open)
100	```

104	
105	The Plan tab in the client reads `PathsView.plan` (= `review/2` copy), `plan_reviewed` and `plan_reviewing` (serve.rs:577-579). I did not read the Swift rendering in `client/`.

111	- `dispatch/tests/first_slice.rs:3442-3500` `revise_writes_the_owners_round_and_sends_it_as_an_objection`: asserts the round file and `Revision`, not a rerun.
112	- No test combines `revise` with a failed review and a rerun. The gap is the test, not only the code.
113	- `dispatch/tests/support/mod.rs:690` fakes `no such run` for an absent run.

116	
117	- `scheduler.rs:10081` `remove_dir_all(&ev.dir)` and `scheduler.rs:10154` `remove_file(path)`: evidence/secret removal. I did not check whether either can reach `review/<n>/` dirs.
118	- `review_subject` ignores `forgotten`, so a forgotten plan artifact on a Complete attempt is still copied. Pre-existing, unrelated to #187 except that a fix touching `review_subject` will meet it.
119	- The `rerun --note` on a plan review is dropped (see 3). The issue does not mention this, but it is the same loss.

122	
123	- I did not run `cargo test`, the dispatch tests, or any Dispatch/Switchboard command, and I did not reproduce the repro.
124	- I did not read the app's planner/reviewer prompts or `src/core/workflow.rs` in full (only `round_file`/snapshot line and `workflow` lookup). I did not confirm how the app edits the copy, or whether a killed run leaves it half-written.

126	- I did not read the rest of `design.md` (3,600 lines), only the sections above; the Milestone status sections are unread.
127	- I did not verify the issue's claims about attempt 2's content (round-1 points, the finalize result) or about the `09:28` timestamp.
128	- Claims about the Claude/Codex sessions are not in scope and were not checked.

Settle by reading the decide path in `dispatch/src/main.rs` and `needs_note` in `dispatch/src/lib.rs`.
136	- [tree] For a failed plan-review attempt, which session is the planning session to name as `WorkflowStart { source }`: `plan/1`'s session, or a session in `review/1.run_sessions` (`scheduler.rs:7710` `note_run_sessions`)? 137	- [tree] Does `dispatch/tests/support/mod.rs` (the fake app) keep the plan copy in its run's `plan` path and read it on `WorkflowStart`, so a test can assert the rerun's copy carries an edit? Settle by reading the fake's workflow handlers near `support/mod.rs:690`.
138	- [tree] How does `client/Sources` render `plan_reviewing`, `plan_round` and the copy's label when a plan review is open with no round (`serve.rs:577-579`)? Settle by reading the Swift view that consumes `PathsView`.

141	- [run] Does the reproduction (review run killed mid-run, then `rerun`) give `no such run` with the Dispatch runner restarted and the app still running, or only after the app restarts? The fake `runs.clear()` models the app losing the run; the real trigger is not confirmed in the tree.

# Spikes

Throwaway crates and scripts that answered the Spike 0 questions in
`docs/design.md` before any product code was written. Each directory has a
README with the commands run, their output, and a recommendation. They are
kept for reference and are not built by the main crate.

| Dir | Question | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `01-claude-resume` | Can Claude Code sessions be captured and resumed? | Yes: `--session-id <uuid>` at launch, `--resume <uuid>` later from any terminal. Transcripts pruned after 30 days unless `cleanupPeriodDays` is raised. |
| `02-process-host` | tmux or own PTYs? | tmux on a private server: sessions outlive the app, reattach works, ~3 ms round trip. PTY adapter kept as fallback and for tests. |
| `03-session-state` | How to know "waiting on you"? | Claude Code hooks (`PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`) via a tiny `switchboard-hook` binary and a Unix socket; OSC 777 text from the raw stream as the hook-free fallback. |
| `05-keychain` | Can secrets live in the Keychain without prompts? | Yes for a bundle signed with a stable identity and identifier: the item ACL is `identifier + certificate`, so rebuilds read silently. Ad-hoc builds prompt per rebuild. |
| `06-pane-size` | Why is the embedded pane wider than the widget? | `window-size manual` ignored the client; `latest` makes the window follow whichever client attached last. Re-applied on launch for servers that outlive the app. |
| `07-clone-session` | Can a session be cloned up to a chosen message? | Yes: copy the transcript prefix before the chosen prompt, substitute a fresh UUID for `sessionId`, save it `0600` beside the original; `--resume <new>` opens the truncated history and the original is untouched. |
| `08-promptbox-embed` | Can Prompt Box be the agent message box? | Yes: same egui 0.36, drawn into a bottom panel unchanged, a `Clipboard` adapter turns Send into a hand-off; needs an embedded mode, a sink port, and focus-scoped shortcuts in promptbox. |
| `09-popout` | Can a session live in a window of its own? | Yes: an immediate viewport drawn from the main frame holds the page, terminal, and side panel; its frame is saved to settings and restored. |
| `10-nunchuk-serial` | Can a nunchuk drive the working set over USB serial? | Yes: one line per button change or stick flick from the Feather, read on a thread that reconnects; round trip 2 to 9 ms. Firmware in `firmware/nunchuk`. |
| `11-gate-sandbox` | Can Dispatch's pipeline commands be confined to the ticket's tree on macOS? | Yes: `sandbox-exec` with `(allow default)`, writes denied except the tree, the attempt directory, the lane's caches and a base set; ~5 ms start-up; a refused write is `EPERM` and a tagged `deny(1)` line in the unified log. `setuid` programs and keychain creation fail inside it. |
| `12-hidden-frames` | Does the frame loop keep running while the window is occluded or minimized? | Not before the fix: with the app hidden, a control query timed out after 10 s and was answered at once on unhide. With the tick and `pump` in `App::logic`, hidden queries answer in 75 to 103 ms (eframe's 100 ms throttle for invisible windows). The sleep and wake cycle is not yet measured. |
| `13-dispatch-service` | Can a Dispatch service be a Switchboard service session, and how is its port read? | Yes: `$SHELL -lc 'exec "$@"' dispatch-service env PORT=<port> npm start` finds `npm`, answers (CRA in 27 s), and is gone with its port 200 ms after `kill-session`. A port is free only if `0.0.0.0`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` all bind: CRA listens on `*`, which a loopback bind does not see. |
| `14-env-exec` | Do a pane's record id and launch token reach a child, so `switchboard-env exec` can resolve its sets? | Yes for a shell grandchild of a tmux pane started with `-e`; the binary's path is covered by `tests/control.rs`. The `aws-vault` form and the no-prompt run under Dispatch's launch flags were not run and are left to the owner. |
| `15-paste-buffer` | Can a multi-line send be bracketed only for a pane that asked for it? | Yes: `load-buffer -` then `paste-buffer -p -r -d` frames the text in `ESC[200~` .. `ESC[201~` for a pane with `bracket_paste_flag` 1 and delivers it bare otherwise; `-r` keeps LF, `-d` leaves no buffer. CR passes through and tmux 3.7c shows ESC as a literal `^[`, so the sender turns CR into LF and removes ESC. `send-keys -H` passes the markers to every pane. Measured on tmux 3.7c. |
| `16-base-pipeline` | Can Dispatch find a merged pull request's merge commit and read the base's pipeline on it? | GitHub, yes: `mergeCommit` on `gh pr list` and `gh pr view`, and the commit's `check-runs` (a short hash works) show the base's run in progress and then finished. Bitbucket's reads were not run (the token could not be read in the run); the adapter follows the documented `merge_commit.hash`, commit `statuses` and pipeline `steps`, with a read by number when a list row lacks the commit; until they are run, a wait on a Bitbucket base pipeline is refused. |
| `18-tmux-argv` | Do `new-session -e` values show in a process listing, and can they reach tmux another way? | Yes, they did: the server keeps the argv of the client that started it. `tmux start-server \; source-file -` with the `new-session` line on stdin keeps every value and the pane command off any argv; cold and warm both work, errors still return, and double-quoted values with `\n` for line breaks round-trip (single quotes lose a line starting with `#`). Measured on tmux 3.7c. |
| `19-structured-ask` | Does a card's answer to a structured ask reach interactive Claude Code as the next user message, sent once, both at the prompt and when held until the turn's `Stop`? | Yes: `Owner answered "<question>": <answer>`, typed as one line, arrived as its own user message once in both cases; a held answer went out only after the `Stop`. Measured on Claude Code 2.1.293 by the ignored gate test `a_structured_answer_arrives_as_the_next_prompt`. |
| `21-evidence-writes` | Which writes reach a stage's evidence directory, outside the agent's cwd, without a prompt? | The Write tool, under the attempt directory's `Edit(//<dir>/**)` rule. Bash `cp`, `mv` and `mkdir` ask, and `--add-dir` does not change that. A Playwright MCP screenshot is refused outside the server's roots unless it runs with `--allow-unrestricted-file-access`. Measured on Claude Code 2.1.295 and `@playwright/mcp@0.0.82`. |
| `22-remote-port` | Can a pinned-TLS HTTP and WebSocket port run on std with every request answered by the frame thread, and what does it cost? | Yes: `rustls` + `rcgen` + `tungstenite` + `mdns-sd`, no Tokio; the frame's share is under 0.25 ms per pass, latency is one frame interval, the pools and the subscriber overflow hold under a stall and an unread socket, Bonjour is seen by `dns-sd`. A 146 MB transcript parses in 290 ms at 575 MB peak, so content work leaves the frame thread. ctime and inode see the file changes mtime and size miss. |
| `04-terminal-view` | Embedded terminal or hand-off? | Hand off agents to Ghostty (`open -na Ghostty --args ... -e cmd`, raise by title); embed `egui_term` for shells, commands, services. |

Findings are folded into `docs/design.md` under "Spike 0 results".

# Facts for #187 (tree HEAD 7fe8949)

The issue and the investigation claim nothing about a browser, platform, crate or protocol outside this tree. Every open question is about this tree, a run, or the owner's machine, so I ran no web searches and wrote no spike. No spike is needed: no question the plan turns on is left to an outside source.

## Settled

Evidence is `file:line` in this worktree.

- Nothing in `dispatch/src/` deletes a plan-review attempt directory or its `plan.md` or `plan.feedback-<n>.md` files.
  - The `remove_dir_all` at `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:10081` removes only `Evidence.dir`, in `drop_evidence`.
  - The `remove_file` at `scheduler.rs:10154` is in `prepare_writes` ("A gate-only command's artifacts made ready", 10136). It is for gate commands, not workflow attempts.
  - The `remove_file` at `scheduler.rs:7642` removes only the just-written owner round file, and only when the app refuses the revise.
  - `retire_replaced` (3578-3605) deletes no directory.
  - So `review/1/joined/plan.md` and its feedback file survive the failure and the rerun. A fix can read them.
- The app can drop a `WorkflowRun` from the project record only through `remove_workflow` (`src/core/workflow.rs:1009-1028`). It refuses while the run `waiting()`. It is also lost on a store reset.
  - `no such run` therefore means the run was removed by a user or the store was reset, not that the app lost it on a plain restart. The tree does not say which happened for the reporter (see For the owner).
  - Evidence: `workflow.rs:1023` is the only `workflows.retain` on records. `core/control.rs:433` and `workflow.rs:54` retain definitions in settings, not runs.
- A `rerun` answer's `--note` is accepted and then dropped for a plan review.
  - `needs_note` (`dispatch/src/lib.rs:101-103`) requires a note only for `finalize`/`revise`, so `decide` for `rerun` takes one. `scheduler.rs:8150` enforces the requirement.

- `RunView` (`control/src/lib.rs:754-767`) carries `id, project, definition, state, round, cap, source, plan, reviewer, planner, op`.
  - It carries no round-snapshot path. Dispatch learns the snapshot directory (`snapshot_dir`, `src/core/workflow.rs:41-48`, `<data dir>/workflows/<run>/round-<n>/`) only by reading the app's data directory itself.
  - `RunView.plan` is the path of the copy Dispatch gave the app at start. In the repro that is `review/1/joined/plan.md`, which Dispatch already holds as `Attempt.artifacts["plan"]`. The snapshot is not needed to find the revised copy.
- `WorkflowStart { source }` must name a live, resumable planning Claude session.
  - The fake app refuses an unknown source with `no such session` and a non-resumable one with `cannot be the planner` (`dispatch/tests/support/mod.rs:397-405`). `design.md` is read as saying the same for the real app.
  - `review_subject` (`scheduler.rs:10534-10548`) returns `a.session` of the chosen attempt. For a workflow attempt `poll_workflow` overwrites `Attempt.session` with the run's `reviewer`/`planner` face (`scheduler.rs:7784-7788`). Picking `review/1` as the subject there would pass a reviewer or planner id as `source`.
  - The planning session to name is `plan/1`'s session. `review/1.run_sessions` (filled by `note_run_sessions`, `scheduler.rs:7710-7735`, keys `reviewer`/`planner`) holds the run's cloned `planner` session. The fake creates that session as "planner planner" (`support/mod.rs:416-423`), and a rerun may use it only if it is still resumable.
- The fake app does not read the plan file on `WorkflowStart`.
  - It stores `plan: plan.clone()` in a `RunView` (`support/mod.rs:430-441`) and never opens the file.
  - A test must therefore assert on the file Dispatch copies (`review/<n>/joined/plan.md`) and on the `plan` path in the recorded `WorkflowStart`, which are Dispatch-side facts.
- The cause is `review_subject` (`scheduler.rs:10534-10548`): it filters `AttemptState::Complete`, so the Failed `review/1` is skipped and `plan/1` is copied (`scheduler.rs:7465-7472`). `rerun_carries` (`scheduler.rs:9382-9390`) returns `""` for a workflow stage, so the rerun question never names a copy.
- Existing tests that constrain a fix:
  - `dispatch/src/ticket.rs:1827-1875` asserts a Failed or Cancelled review copy is not shown as the plan (1856-1864).
  - `ticket.rs:1797` asserts a Failed plan attempt is skipped as an input.
  - `dispatch/tests/first_slice.rs:3257-3287` and `3817-3831` cover the failed-review rerun without checking which plan was copied.
  - `first_slice.rs:3442-3500` covers revise without a rerun.
  - No test combines revise, a failed review and a rerun.
- `show`'s `files:` block (`dispatch/src/serve.rs:538-600`, `main.rs:980-995`) takes `review` from the latest workflow attempt that has artifacts (`serve.rs:564-568`).
  - After the rerun that is `review/2`, so `plan_rounds` lists nothing for the owner's round in `review/1`.
  - `print_answered` (`main.rs:1176-1198`) still prints the `revise` note while the decision stays on the ticket, so the note is visible there.
- Rendering of `plan_reviewing`/`plan_round` in `client/Sources` was not read. It is a presentation question for the planner, not a fact the plan turns on.

- Whether a half-written `review/1/joined/plan.md` is possible after a killed run (the file is edited in place by the app).
  - Tried: reading `start_workflow`/`revise` in Dispatch. Dispatch only copies and reads it. The app's edit path is in `src/core/workflow.rs`, which I did not read in full.
  - Not settled because the answer needs the app's write behaviour or a killed run, which is outside the smallest experiment the plan turns on.
  - Build to: copy `review/1/joined/plan.md` as it is, and write the new attempt's copy with the same copy call. This is safe either way and needs no new atomic write: a partial file is the owner's call to inspect, and the rerun question names which copy is used.
  - If favourable, nothing more is needed. If unfavourable, nothing more is needed either, because the owner can see the named copy.
- Whether the planning session `plan/1` names is still resumable at rerun time (needed for `WorkflowStart.source`).
  - Tried: reading `start_workflow` and the fake. The real check lives in the app and needs a live session.
  - Build to: keep passing `plan/1`'s session as `source`, as the first attempt does today. If it is gone, the existing `Reply::Failed` branch (`scheduler.rs:7522` onward) already fails the attempt with a reason and asks `rerun`/`park`. The plan must add no fallback to another session.
- Whether `Revision` entries on `review/1` can be re-sent to a new app run.
  - The `WorkflowObject { run, round, text }` body targets an existing run (`revise`, `scheduler.rs:7565-7650`). Whether the app accepts an objection on a fresh run at round 1 was not checked.
  - Build to: the plan must not depend on resending the owner's note. Starting the rerun from the revised copy carries the revision itself. The note stays available as the answered `revise` decision.

## For the owner

Questions of fact only the owner can observe. Neither answer changes what the plan builds, and none blocks it.

- Does `review/1/joined/plan.md` on the reporter's machine still hold the revision (diff against `plan/1/joined/plan.md` and `review/2/joined/plan.md`), and does `review/1/joined/plan.feedback-2.md` exist with the owner's note?
  - If yes: the fix can read both from the failed attempt, and the issue's repro is confirmed on disk.
  - If no: the fix still starts the rerun from the newest copy Dispatch holds (the failed attempt's copy or `plan/1`) and names it in the question and in `show`.
  - The plan builds the same either way.
- Did the Switchboard app's project record lose the run (a removed run, a store reset, or a changed data directory) between the review's start and the `rerun` answer?
  - If yes: `no such run` is explained, and the plan may add a test that models it with `runs.clear()` (`support/mod.rs:690`).
  - If no (runner restart only): the cause is outside this tree. The plan still builds the same fix, because a failed attempt of any reason has to hand its copy to the rerun.
- Does attempt 2's plan carry the content the issue describes (every question open, an owner answer contradicted, two of three round-1 points already fixed in the revised copy)?
  - If yes: the plan has a worked example for its test fixtures, with the client's text replaced.
  - If no: the plan builds the same. The content check is the owner's own ticket and does not bear on the mechanism.
